answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to anchor its signing key to a speaker-biometric nullifier. During onboarding, a verifier sends an uncached sonnet for a human sponsor to read aloud, checks spectral liveness, and stores a locality-sensitive hash of the vocal embedding to block duplicate voices. Attackers must supply a distinct human speaker per identity. However, neural voice cloning or wind noise on a coastal jetty can spoof checks or skew embeddings.
